excerpt: You can use Shopify POS to sell your products in person in retail stores, popups, and other locations. Shopify POS is available for only iOS and Android devices.
Shopify POS syncs with Shopify to track your orders and inventory across your retail locations, online store, and other active sales channels.
Migrating and integrating QuickBooks Desktop POS with Shopify POS
Scale your business with a centralized back office that supports 1,000+ locations.
Draft orders, multichannel gift cards, reporting and analytics and more.
Integrate with your existing software and easily customize with low-code and no-code options.
Manage and fulfill in-store pickup orders directly from Shopify POS.
Make sales in store and ship directly to customers from anywhere you have inventory. Taxes and shipping rates are automatically calculated at checkout.
Accept exchanges for purchases made online or at another location and your inventory will be updated instantly.
Manage and fulfill local delivery orders placed online directly from your Shopify POS.
Attach QR codes to products so customers can use their smartphone to learn more and purchase online.
Send customers an email with items they were interested in but didn’t purchase in store.
Surface shipping orders for fulfillment in POS so staff can pick, pack and ship orders, including purchasing and printing shipping labels.
Track and assign inventory at every location that syncs in real time across POS, online store, and every sales channel.
Accept incoming shipments from other locations or suppliers in Shopify POS, manually or with a barcode scanner.
Use Quick counts with a barcode scanner to update stock quantities on the spot in Shopify POS.
Create, send, and track supplier purchase orders from Shopify admin.
Use Sidekick, Shopify’s AI assistant, to get reordering suggestions based on sales velocity and seasonality.
Ask Sidekick to recommend stock transfers between locations based on performance trends, and create them for you automatically.
Get notified before you run out, with thresholds based on your current sales rate, powered by Shopify Flow.
Specify when your staff would need manager approval for actions like applying discounts or editing taxes.
Assign custom roles to store staff ensuring they have the correct permissions.
Attribute sales to staff members for commissions or kudos.
Give staff members unique PINs to log into POS.
Turn your smartphone into a checkout for on-the-go selling with Tap to Pay.
Add POS Hub to connect your peripherals to your tablet with rock-solid USB connectivity and built-in device monitoring.
Tap to Pay works with contactless credit and debit cards, smartwatches, Apple Pay, Google Pay, and digital wallets for fast and smooth checkouts.
WiFi and cellular data connectivity let you take contactless payments, look up customer profiles, or view inventory with a smartphone on the sales floor.
Use Shopify POS to create a cart for each customer. You can also modify the cart, for example, by adding or removing products or applying a discount.
Customizing your Shopify POS with the POS editor
Using Shopify POS offline
Collecting tips with the Shopify POS
Changing the smart grid in the Shopify POS app
With Shopify POS UI extensions, you can add custom functionality directly into Shopify's point-of-sale interface. For example, you can offer loyalty program enrollment at checkout
There are three types of targets: Tiles: Used to display tiles on the smart grid. Actions: Used to launch modals... Blocks: Used to display custom sections within screens.
Extensions can also query the GraphQL Admin API directly using standard fetch() calls.
Consistent design: Automatically match Shopify's design system and receive updates.
Use Shopify CLI to scaffold your extension with the essential configuration and files.
For example, shopify.storage persists data between sessions, shopify.toast displays feedback messages, and shopify.action.presentModal() launches full-screen workflows.

A retailer noted that the Shopify POS site doesn't say it supports a barcode scanner, though the video shows one in use. They called scanning a deal breaker for any serious inventory, especially with size/color variants, because of error risk and checkout speed.
One commenter asked whether Shopify POS lacks a barcode scanner. They suggested the device camera could act as a scanner with no extra hardware.

An agency commenter said budget clients repeatedly chose Magento over Shopify for its finer-grained control. They found it frustrating that Shopify could release a POS system but still fall short on things like complex sales reports.
One commenter called combining POS, inventory management and merchant services in one product a game changer, but said it still needs chip (EMV) support.

A Canadian merch-booth seller was surprised Shopify POS had no Interac support, given Shopify is from Canada. They said more storefronts there accept Interac debit than credit cards, so stores would turn away business without it.
A commenter from the Bitcoin world called Shopify POS's 2.1% + 30 cents transaction fees ridiculous.
A longtime fan said they have praised Shopify to clients and others many times. They said its products and services keep getting better across the board and called the POS launch excellent work.

A development agency director said they can't use Shopify, including the new POS, for clients until products support custom fields. Their example was a wine store needing vintage and alcohol volume, and they called the technology useless to them until then.
A user reported an integer overflow in Shopify POS that was breaking the inventory count for products.
